profile.name: Jim Simons
profile.description:
James Harris Simons (1938–2024) was a mathematician, quantitative investor and philanthropist. He earned a mathematics degree at MIT and a doctorate at UC Berkeley, worked in codebreaking and academic mathematics, and chaired Stony Brook’s mathematics department from 1968 to 1978. His research with Shiing-Shen Chern produced the Chern–Simons theory used in mathematics and physics.

He left academia to establish Monometrics in 1978, renamed Renaissance Technologies in 1982. Renaissance developed investment strategies based on mathematical models; its Medallion Fund began in 1988. Simons retired as chief executive in 2010. With Marilyn Simons, he co-founded the Simons Foundation in 1994 and supported scientific research and mathematics education. He died on May 10, 2024. Autopilot’s namesake tracker follows the firm’s public filings rather than trades personally made by Simons.

profile.description:
Alejandro Lopez-Lira is an assistant professor of finance at the University of Florida’s Warrington College of Business. His research studies asset pricing, machine learning and the use of language models in financial analysis. He earned finance graduate degrees at the University of Pennsylvania, completing his PhD in 2020.

On Autopilot, he designs portfolios published under Dr. Lira’s AI Finance Labs, including strategies using GPT and other language models. Model backtests, actual portfolio results and academic claims are separate types of evidence.
